audience.programmeDescription: Health and Society studies how behaviour, social conditions, environments and public decisions shape health. Psychology, sociology, economics and research methods support prevention, healthier communities and health policy.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The three UCR programmes approach these interests through population health and social policy, inequality and public institutions, or behavioural evidence and public communication. Dedicated nutrition, health demography, healthy-neighbourhood fieldwork, systematic health-intervention design and the required thesis remain important differences.

selectedCourseDescriptions.name: Econometrics
selectedCourseDescriptions.text: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

selectedCourseDescriptions.name: Governance of Sustainability
selectedCourseDescriptions.text: This course examines sustainability through the lens of governance: “a process of rule-making and collective decision-making that includes both governmental and non-governmental actors in shaping public policy” (Fenger & Bekkers, 2016). Taking this lens, we ask questions such as how are sustainability policies on the local, national, and international level made and enforced? Which actors represent which interests, and which are most influential? How is public opinion on sustainability shaped, and how does public opinion shape politics? What, at the end of the day, determines effective policy for sustainability? By the end of this course, you will have gained a deep appreciation of the complexity of the governance dimension of sustainability, and have developed the theoretical and practical understanding to critically assess mainstream policy decisions.
